intent: Replace raw operator-token browser cookies with revocable opaque sessions under accepted ADR-0012 and ADR-0013, while preserving Bearer clients, intentional URL hand-off, exact read-only refusals, loopback HTTP, and supported proxy/LAN deployment modes.
programme: Accepted ADR-0012 and ADR-0013 settle the browser-session design and its private-proxy, token-rotation, read-only and onboarding corrections. Accepted ADR-0014 bounds expired and revoked session metadata after the operator's 30-day ruling. The former T-0158 universal X-Forwarded-Proto conclusion is refuted by normal Next request handling; the synthetic NextRequest probe did not model the server path. Raw-token cookies, one-year lifetime, no individual revocation and token-bearing boot logs remain live findings. T-0179 dependency cleanup closed with every hosted implementation and closure job green at dev@b2be4a64. Remote branches are dev and main, with PR #157 alone open; local worktrees with unique or ignored state remain preserved. This is the security prerequisite before the unfinished T-0164 reconnaissance and T-0165 Phase 2 plan.
invariants: Mint 256-bit opaque browser secrets, store only hashes in separate auth_sessions SQLite storage, and keep existing Bearer precedence. Session creation, lookup or migration failure fails closed; old raw-token cookies are cleared.

Enforce 30-minute inactivity and 12-hour absolute expiry at exact boundaries. Only qualified interactive navigation or user action renews activity. Atomic renewal cannot revive an expired or revoked row; polling, prefetch and streams do not renew.

Mint one process-owned boot generation and key; production proxy, routes and streams observe the same values. Restored rows or token rotation invalidate sessions. Prove this in a built app before implementation; if it fails, stop for design review.

Pin exact Origin and cookie transport to PS_PUBLIC_ORIGIN. Retain direct loopback HTTP, require HTTPS for supported network access by default, and permit only explicit insecure LAN HTTP or isolated private proxy modes. Headers supplied by a caller cannot establish transport trust.

Preserve intentional GET token hand-off, add exact POST sign-in, DELETE self sign-out and credential-gated list/revoke routes. Clear legacy cookies, avoid browser credential storage and remove token-bearing boot logs or onboarding copy.

Under PS_READ_ONLY, allow only the ADR's exact auth lifecycle writes and qualified navigation renewal. Continue refusing application writes. Recheck session validity before every protected stream emission and on quiet ticks, aborting upstream on invalidation.
Under accepted ADR-0014, remove only rows unusable for at least 30 days, at the next sign-in, in the same transaction as insertion. An active row is never eligible; failed cleanup issues no cookie.

Keep Windows and Git Bash development, existing test names, the complete unchanged-tree gate, responsive browser journeys, committed-tree sweep and all hosted jobs. Protected ADRs change only after operator acceptance.
notes: The original 2026-09-13 synthetic NextRequest protocol probe was not representative of normal Next handling. ADR-0012 refutes its universal X-Forwarded-Proto claim. This task uses PS_PUBLIC_ORIGIN and the proxy-isolation modes in accepted ADR-0012/0013; no security decision is based on client-supplied forwarding or Host headers alone. Static inspection of the Next 16.3.6 production bundle found a shared Turbopack runtime and module cache, but did not prove one boot generation across live proxy, route and stream requests. That production proof is the first implementation gate. Existing proxy-auth and read-only tests include raw-cookie and source-text assumptions; amend their expectations through a different author without losing test identities. Independent R2 REVIEWER session 01a0e468-e114-7dc2-8033-00d272b1bf9f authorised on 2026-09-27 a narrow T-0161 copied-fixture amendment: copy the newly imported network-boundary.mjs alongside the existing three deploy files; preserve every assertion and test name. This corrects a harness launch error, not a failed product assertion; one separate sandbox ENOMEM failure still needs an escalated rerun. R3 oracle amendments were independently authored and their test-name identities recorded; accepted ADR-0012/0013/0014 govern the final boundary.
rollback: Restore the old auth code only through a forward-compatible migration and new dev commit; never drop an auth_sessions table with live rows. Keep Bearer access and a documented recovery route if session storage is unavailable.
